environmental.storage-temp: -40 C to 70 C in shipping container

features.macsec: inline MACsec on all ports at all speeds
features.redundancy: full hardware redundancy - Routing Engines, power supplies and fans
features.timing: 1PPS and 10 MHz SMB input and output, ToD and BITS RJ45, GM/PTP SFP (1-GbE/10-GbE); BITS and GM/PTP currently reserved for future use per the guide

performance.throughput: 4.8 Tbps system capacity; up to 12x400 Gbps or 48x100 Gbps ports (three LMICs)

physical.depth-with-brackets: 782 mm over cable-management brackets, air filter and handles (Table 22)
physical.weight: 32 kg fully loaded (two REs, two LMICs); 16 kg without FRUs (Table 22)

platform.asic: Juniper Trio 6 (one YT ASIC per LMIC)

configs.description: Chassis only - what you spec before deciding what goes in it. The 2 slot bays are EMPTY; fans, psus, res are populated. Enough to power on and reach the box, which is the question most people ask first and the one `default` used to answer with whatever the drawing happened to be populated with.

gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing resolving the module envelopes against the drawn apertures - Table 22 states 203.5 mm module and 73.5 mm PSU envelopes while the photographed apertures measure 197.6 and 66.0; the bays and module faces are both drawn at the aperture and the envelopes live in each contract's attrs. That reconciliation is a judgement (rails hidden behind the panel), not a measurement, and this gap is its record.

geometry for the optional JNP-FLTRDR-2RU cover and JNP-AIRFLTR-2RU filter that bolt over the front face (Table 22 gives envelopes; no straight-on image exists in the intake). Not modelled; the bare front is the photographed configuration.

a corrected vendor dimension for the fan module - Table 22's row reads 0.31 x 5.62 x 0.31 in, dimensionally impossible for a module holding two 80 mm fans; the model carries the photographed 82.0 x 85.5 aperture and the table's 143 mm depth.
the 400GbE-configuration chassis power totals (guide Table 26) - the rows fell outside the docling text layer; only the 100GbE Table 25 totals are carried.
the MX304 transceiver list - the guide points at the external Hardware Compatibility Tool and no document in the intake carries the table.
the removable front brackets carrying the RE 0 / LMIC0 / RE1/LMIC2 / LMIC1 slot legends, should ears-and-brackets modelling ever be wanted; with ears unmodelled the chassis prints no slot names.
`attrs.platform.cpu`, `attrs.platform.memory` (profile `networking` - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml) - unlocks the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 9 bays (front 4, rear 5) - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
the Nautobot exporter is not importable - unlocks NetBox / Nautobot device-type export

badge-strip.note: photo - the dark strip right of the module columns (402.9-440.8) carries two columns of three square vent apertures, the JUNIPER / MX 304 badge mid-height, and the front ESD socket at its top with the symbol beside it. Positions are photo-fractions, approximate

chassis.note: datasheet-table - Table 22: chassis 3.5 x 17.36 x 24.01 in (88.9 x 440.8 x 610 mm), 2RU; 78.2 cm deep over cable-management brackets and handles. The chassis-description prose says 17.63 in (44.8 cm) wide - a 0.7 cm disagreement with Table 22; the table is carried and the prose recorded here. Fully loaded 32 kg, bare 16 kg. Ears are NOT MODELLED by project convention; the modelled body is the 440.8 mm between the flange folds, and the slot labels (RE 0, LMIC0, RE1/LMIC2, LMIC1) are printed on the REMOVABLE BRACKETS the photographs show, so they appear nowhere on this body - recorded so their absence is not read as an omission

color.note: photo - medium grey chassis (#8b8f94), bright aluminium module plates, pale blue ejector levers, Juniper orange fan furniture

esd.note: guide Figure 11 (ESD Points) - one point on the front badge strip top, one on the rear right above the earthing plate. Both are plain sockets in the photographs

fan-strips.note: photo - each fan bay's chassis strip to its right prints the fan icon, the bay number and the bicolour status lamp (Table 12: green blinking = hardware init complete, green steady = ok, yellow steady = faulty). The fourth strip position at the far right shares the ground zone

front-cover.note: not modelled - the optional front cover with air filter (JNP-FLTRDR-2RU + JNP-AIRFLTR-2RU, Table 22) bolts over the entire front face; the guide documents replacement procedures for both. Modelled configuration is the bare front as photographed; see gaps

grounding.note: guide grounding specifications + photo - two threaded holes for M6 pan-head screws on 16 mm centres at the rear right, under the earth symbol; the protective earthing terminal bracket attaches here. Modelled as juniper/mx304-ground-plate

lifecycle.note: none-announced - searched "Juniper MX304 end of life end of sale" 2026-08-26; the third-party EOL trackers list no dates and the 2022 NANOG thread names the MX304 as the successor replacing the MX204 and MX10003. Absence of the announcement is the finding

other-faces.note: near-blank by evidence - no source shows the top, bottom or side faces; each carries only an estimated mounting-rail band so the capability chain counts it as drawn, sized from Table 22. Axis conventions per viewer3d.js: LEFT view x = 0 is the REAR, RIGHT view x = 0 is the FRONT, top and bottom y = 0 at the FRONT

power.note: guide Table 25, the vendor's own per-module table at two ambients for the 3.2 Tbps two-RE + two-LMIC 100GbE configuration: REs 49/59 W each, SFB+CB+PMB 155/228 (chassis internals, not a FRU here), LMICs 318/410 each with transceivers, fans 48/90 each; total chassis power 1033 W at 25 C and 1436 W at 46 C. Those totals are carried as the device figures with that scope in power-envelope; Table 26 gives the 400GbE configuration and its totals fell outside this extraction's text layer - not carried rather than guessed

rear.note: photo (mx304-rear-ac-high) - stacked PSU bays at x 10.9 (PSU 0 above PSU 1, labels printed vertically on the chassis strip right of them), the fixed timing strip at 84-116, three 82.0 mm fan bays EVENLY spaced at x 116.4, 225.4 and 334.5 (26.9 mm label strips between and after, each printing the bay's number, lamp and fan icon), and the earthing plate and rear ESD socket at the right end. A FIRST READING PUT FAN 1 AT 213.4 AND CALLED THE SPACING ASYMMETRIC - it had mis-assigned fan 1's edges to its grille internals; the DC rear photograph (independent shot, same chassis) and a zoom on the strip between fans 1 and 2 both give the even layout, and the reviewer's instinct that routers do not stagger their fans was what triggered the re-measure. The rear drawing (g101368 family) was measured too but its verticals mix module internals at this threshold and were not used for positions

scale.note: photo + drawing, cross-anchored per axis - the guide front drawing (g101366) measures aspect 5.58 against the rack face's 5.43 and is internally inconsistent in x by ~1.5%, and the front photograph is ~16% COMPRESSED in y (near-axis studio shot) while consistent in x. So: front x positions come from the photograph at 4.058 px/mm anchored to the 440.8 body, front y positions from the drawing anchored to the 88.9 height. The rear photograph is near-isotropic (3%) and rear positions come from it at 4.236 px/mm (x) / 4.106 (y). Feature sizes come from the registry and Table 22 throughout

slots.note: drawing + photo - four half-width apertures in two columns of two: RE 0 above LMIC 0 on the left, RE 1/LMIC2 above LMIC 1 on the right (guide Figure 2 callouts name all four). Rows y 4.1-43.8 and 44.6-84.3 off the drawing; columns x 1.2-198.8 and 205.3-402.9 off the photograph, separated by the centre rail. A one-RE system may seat a THIRD LMIC in the RE 1/LMIC2 slot (guide Figure 3 shows it; hardware overview text: "You can also add a third LMIC into one of the Routing Engine slots"). The 197.6 mm apertures take 203.5 mm module envelopes - the modules carry insert: for the difference

sources.note: MX304 Universal Routing Platform Hardware Guide (figures g101366/ g101368/g101334/g101624 among others), MX304 datasheet (mx304-datasheet.pdf), Juniper image-library studio photographs mx304-front-high, mx304-rear-ac-high and mx304-rear-dc-high, and the NetBox devicetype-library MX304 elevations. No mechanical drawing was available

timing.note: photo + guide timing topic - SMB quad at x 98.6/107.1, y 11.6/22.2 (rows 10 MHz above 1PPS, columns OUT left / IN right per the rotated legends), BITS RJ45 centred at 101.9, 35.6, ToD at 101.3, 55.4, and the GM/PTP SFP cage VERTICAL at 100.1, 74.9 with its link lamp to the left. The guide NOTE says BITS and GM/PTP are currently unsupported and reserved for future use - carried in attrs. GM/PTP supports 1-GbE and 10-GbE optics per the same topic
